:::{#thm-kolmogorov-upper-bound}
#### A string is never much more complex than its length

There is a constant $c$ such that every binary string $x$ of length $n$ has

$$K(x \mid n) \le n + c$$

and, when $n \ge 1$,

$$K(x) \le n + 2 \log_2 n + c.$$

:::

::: {.proof}
For the first bound, the program "print the next $n$ digits"
followed by the $n$ digits of $x$ outputs $x$.
Because $U$ is given $n$, the program needs no marker to show where it ends,
and its fixed part has some length $c_1$.
So $K(x \mid n) \le n + c_1$.

For the second bound, the program must also describe $n$
in a way that shows where the description ends.
Write $n$ in binary, which takes $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$ digits,
repeat each digit twice, and end with the pair $01$.
This takes $2 \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 4 \le 2 \log_2 n + 4$ digits.
A program that reads this description of $n$ and then prints the next $n$ digits
has length at most $n + 2 \log_2 n + 4 + c_2$
for a constant $c_2$.
Take $c = \max(c_1, c_2 + 4)$.
@cover2006elements [section 14.2] prove both bounds.

:::
